cadence.ninety_day_route_target_semantics: planning_capacity_reference_not_quota, derived from data/cadence/policy.json: 2 new pages per week over 13 weeks. The prior 4500 was a capacity aspiration with no relationship to the declared cadence, and this property already has 3362 pages producing 2 citations, so volume is not the constraint.
cadence.cadence_policy_authority: data/cadence/policy.json is the single source of truth for publishing rate (new_pages_per_week). Every figure here is a per-run safety cap that can only lower that allowance, never raise it. max_new_pages_per_day sat at 50 with two scheduled runs a day against a declared 2 per week, which is how 52 unaccepted editorial URLs accumulated at roughly 26x the cap; it is now the weekly figure so no number in this file contradicts the policy.

strategy_targets.route_target_90_days_semantics: planning_capacity_reference_not_quota, derived from data/cadence/policy.json: new_pages_per_week (2) over floor(refresh_window_days/7) = 13 weeks. data/cadence/policy.json is the single source of truth; every figure here is a safety cap that can only lower that allowance, never raise it. This sat at 4500 after cadence.ninety_day_route_target was corrected to 26, so the same contract file stated two different 90-day route targets.

quality.legacy_duplicate_policy: report_and_bounded_repair; legacy backlog does not make unrelated releases permanently unreleasable
quality.new_page_policy: render_and_quality_check_before_write; thin or near-duplicate candidates are skipped with receipts
quality.repair_policy: only count a repair when the page content actually changes and passes the same substance and duplicate gate
